verdicts.note: Two-term incumbent with the office since 1994 in every rank up to chief criminal deputy (S1), reelected 62.4% in 2022 (S11, S12). -2 high is the maximal proven-record case. Minor: the basis's union-endorsement clause is supported by S4/S5, not the cited S1/S11/S12, but the score stands on the cited tenure evidence.

Attacked toward 0 because he runs co-responder mental health and opioid outreach (S1, S11). But his own framing is 'education, enforcement and accountability', with treatment people are 'willing to do' plus being 'held accountable' (S3), and his 2022 goal of 50-55 deputies to restore a proactive team for burglaries and drug houses (S11) is staffing-and-enforcement. -1 medium is right; not -2 given the services record.

Attacked toward 0: he is a career law-enforcement professional (Marine MP, seven years a county deputy, Langley chief since 2022, S1). But this is his first run for office, against a two-term incumbent, and he has not run a sheriff's office or jail (S1). +1 medium is a fair challenger placement; +2 would overstate an outsider profile.

Attacked toward 0: he also wants more SWAT, hostage and K9/drone training and more deputy availability (S4, S7). But his distinguishing proposals are on the prevention/services side: telling 'a crime and a call for help' apart and expanding mental-health capacity (S4), routing some behavioral-health calls to social workers (S7), and a victim advocacy unit (S4). +1 medium reflects the mix; the basis already notes the tactical training.
